qualification: Startup counts free slots below the inherited soft limit without opening a descriptor. It requires 32 slots before loading optional libraries, consuming the token, or creating owned state. The controller verifies refusal at 31 slots; all admitted production launches run at 32 free slots.

Startup and the single-threaded guardian check capacity before their explicit open, openat, fopen, opendir, pipe2, socket and eventfd calls. The ready protocol worker retains its existing mutex/reserve operation admission. No limit is raised and no inherited descriptor is closed to obtain capacity.

With only the live authenticated guardian constrained to zero, graceful worker shutdown retains its unchanged ownership journal and exits 125. Fresh same-boot reconciliation preserves the known interrupted exit 137 and terminal record bytes.

With only that guardian constrained to zero, a SIGSEGV directed to its own authenticated worker reaches a ptrace stop. Guarded task-identity inspection refuses; guardian exit 1 activates EXITKILL, retains ownership, and a fresh launch reconciles the interrupted job with unknown exit status. Original task identities are observed dead before takeover; the command witness is written once.

Once ptrace supervision is active, fatal guardian errors bypass generic runtime cleanup and retain ownership evidence until ordinary takeover proves tasks gone. A local simulated task-identity ENOMEM with spare descriptors previously removed the journal; the corrected code preserves it and reconciles without replay.

A test-only Linux interposer exits 93 if an actual exhausted libc allocation is attempted, modeling firmware forced-abort risk without invoking a host crash collector. Both previous-binary guardian cases reach 93; guarded cases pass. The interposer is absent from signed packages and was not used on either TV.

Both TVs also passed the prior eleven production resource checks using their exact installed ordinary worker bytes. Per-TV locks, identity/runtime/signing pins, unique requests and independent 300-second managed rescue were retained. Cleanup verified scopes, helpers, jobs, SDK loopback, enrollment and protected hashes.

prior_failed_trial.failure: An existing command-fault job reached its 2000ms timeout and returned timed_out/137. The original controller did not capture iteration or phase timings.
prior_failed_trial.resolution: Not reproduced by the subsequent instrumented full trial; root cause remains unresolved. No worker code or timing threshold was changed to obtain that pass.

diagnostic_controller.changes: Private acceptance controller records per-iteration admission/end-to-end timing; slow or mismatched results include job/fault state and read-only owned-process snapshots.

limits: The first final-candidate QN90A full trial failed one existing two-second command-fault job timeout after the first eleven checks. The subsequent full instrumented trial passed unchanged thresholds; latency tails are recorded, but the initial timeout is unexplained and broader timing/endurance qualification remains open.

This does not protect dynamic ELF-loader allocation before main; hardware refusal leaves 31 free slots for that boundary. It does not establish an atomic guarantee against an unrelated concurrent prlimit change between capacity inspection and syscall.
Guardian exhaustion deliberately retains the journal for ordinary same-boot takeover instead of claiming cleanup completed with zero descriptors. No unknown command is retried.

The simulated task-identity ENOMEM is locally qualified only; no TV-wide memory exhaustion was injected. These are bounded separate-worker trials, with managed still selected. Concurrent memory/process pressure, wider storage stalls, remaining lifecycle faults, endurance and native-default observation remain open.

Native-only capability entry is still unqualified; the .NET entry bridge, worker fallback and independent rescue remain deployed. No reboot, standby, global-policy, persistent file-capability or SMACK-rule change occurred.
